text:
Smoke testing the router deliberately goes over HTTP against a running server rather than importing anything from src/.

Extracting the ROUTER_API_KEY auth helpers out of src/router/server.ts into a unit-testable module was proposed and rejected. Stavros wanted a test that proves Anthropic actually answers end to end, not one that proves middleware logic in isolation, so the refactor bought nothing for the goal and was dropped in favour of tests/smoke.js.

Worth knowing before proposing it again: server.ts genuinely cannot be imported as-is. At module load it throws on an empty ROUTER_API_KEY, reads process.argv via parseArgs(), builds the Express app, then calls startRouter(), which does interactive readline OAuth prompts, process.exit(1) on failure, and app.listen(). Any in-process test of that file requires splitting the entry point from the app construction first. That is a real refactor, not a small one, and nobody has asked for it.

Authenticated proxy mode cannot start unattended, which blocks containerised and service-managed deployment.

Setting ROUTER_API_KEY force-disables bearer passthrough (src/router/server.ts). startRouter() then finds no usable credentials if .oauth-tokens.json is absent or unparseable, and drops into the interactive OAuth readline prompt, so app.listen() is never reached and /health never answers. Observed empirically while building the Docker smoke harness: a corrupt token file hangs startup until something else times out.

Consequence: any Docker or systemd deployment of authenticated proxy mode needs a valid token file pre-seeded on disk, since the container cannot complete the browser flow. tests/smoke-docker.sh works around it by validating the token JSON before starting compose and failing fast with a clear message.

Raised with Stavros during planning and consciously left unfixed for now; the smoke test work was the priority. A real fix would be a non-interactive startup mode that exits with a clear error instead of prompting when no TTY is attached.
